title: Context shouldn't disappear when the meeting ends: what Zoom's Unified Context Layer means for IT
summary: Most organizations have more collaboration tools than ever, yet context behind decisions, action items, and customer history disappears the moment the conversation ends. At Zoomtopia 2026, Zoom introduced the Unified Context Layer to help change that.
body_markdown:
Standup on[Zoom](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/virtual-meetings/) . Vendor call in Google Meet. Engineering sync in Microsoft Teams. For most IT organizations, that's just the regular schedule.


Every one of those conversations generates decisions, commitments, and history that someone needs later. In most environments, all of it is scattered across platforms, buried in personal notes apps, or gone the moment the call ends.


IT decision-makers know this problem intimately. Collaboration tool sprawl means more places to search, more handoffs to manage, and more context to reconstruct by hand, without necessarily making anyone more productive. The tools work. The question is whether the organization is getting value out of the time invested in those conversations, or generating more places for information to get lost.


Deloitte found that 94% of employees report experiencing meeting challenges at some point in the meeting lifecycle, from preparation to execution to follow-up.* Teams report spending more time coordinating work than doing it. Decisions that should take hours stretch into days because the context lives in one platform while the conversation happens in another.


## Where context breaks down for IT


For IT teams managing collaboration environments, these problems are not abstract. They are the daily reality. Five patterns show where the value leaks out, and each one lands on IT's desk.


### Context dies between platforms


An employee takes a customer call on[Zoom Phone](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/voip-phone/) , discusses requirements in a follow-up meeting, and then manually recreates those details in the CRM. Every handoff is a chance for context to degrade. Multiply that across thousands of interactions per week, and the cumulative information loss is significant. Work does not happen in one system, and connecting context across applications and workflows is the kind of problem IT leaders are asked to solve at scale.


### Decisions evaporate after meetings


A decision gets made in a meeting. Attendees agree on next steps. Then the meeting ends, and those decisions live only in the memories of the people who were there. Without structured capture and follow-through, decisions can decay into ambiguity, leading teams to revisit the same topics weeks later. If your teams have ever sent a follow-up email just to get everyone back on the same page about something that was already agreed to, you have felt this problem firsthand.


### Voice stays isolated from the rest of the business


Phone calls carry some of the most valuable business intelligence in the organization, from customer escalations to vendor negotiations, but in most environments, voice data never connects to the rest of the collaboration stack. The insights stay locked in one channel while decisions are made in another.


### AI tools operate in silos


When one AI assistant summarizes meetings, another drafts messages, and a third searches documents, none of them share what the others know. Employees end up becoming the integration layer themselves, copying context from one tool to another just to keep things moving. Deloitte found that even as workforce access to AI tools expanded by 50% in a single year, fewer than 60% of workers with access actually used those tools in their daily workflow.† Fragmentation makes that gap worse, not better: the tool exists, the information is technically there, but nobody can find it when they need it.


### Adoption plateaus below the value threshold


Organizations invest in collaboration platforms and watch adoption dashboards trend upward. But healthy login rates do not necessarily mean employees are getting business value from the investment. When collaboration is disconnected from the workflows where business outcomes are produced (the CRM update, the project plan, the customer follow-up) the collaboration itself becomes overhead instead of a catalyst.


For IT leaders, all of this adds up to the same handful of recurring headaches: app sprawl, rising costs from stitching together point solutions, fragmented security and compliance postures, and slower onboarding every time a new tool gets bolted on. And because an IT decision-maker is buying for the workforce, not for themselves, every one of those headaches has to translate into a business case that goes beyond "better governance." It has to solve a problem employees feel, at scale, with a measurable impact.


## What the Unified Context Layer actually does


Zoom's Unified Context Layer connects decisions, relationships, and history from business conversations with information in documents, data, and general knowledge. Instead of asking people (or AI agents) to reconstruct context from scratch, the layer brings together meeting and chat conversations with near real-time activity across Zoom and connected third-party applications, giving people and AI agents access to business context that might otherwise be lost or siloed.


Think of it this way: every meeting, chat message, phone call, and document your organization produces contains context that matters to the next step in a workflow. The Unified Context Layer is the infrastructure that makes context accessible, within the security and admin controls IT manages.


Those capabilities show up for your teams in several ways.


### Find answers without retracing every conversation


Tracking down a decision or a detail often means manually searching through multiple apps and message threads. **Agentic Search** helps surface answers from across Zoom Meetings, Phone, and[Chat](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/team-chat/) , as well as more than 40 third-party applications — including ServiceNow, Workday, Google Drive, and Microsoft OneDrive — so teams can get answers swiftly, regardless of where the conversation happened. *(Available now.)*


For IT, this means fewer support tickets that boil down to "where was that decision made?" and less time spent being the human search engine for the rest of the organization.


### From meeting context to completed work


The biggest promise of the Unified Context Layer is closing the gap between what happens in a conversation and what happens after it. Three[My Notes](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/ai-assistant/features/ai-note-taking/) capabilities help do that directly.


**My Notes workflows** can route meeting summaries and action items into the tools where follow-up actually happens, including Zoom Chat and Salesforce. Pre-built workflows cover sales, marketing, and IT use cases, and teams can build custom ones by describing what to automate in natural language. No separate workflow builder required. *(Expected October 2026.)*


This is the difference between "the meeting produced a summary" and "the meeting produced a CRM update, a task assignment, and a follow-up message in the channel where the team works." The context layer connects one to the other.


**Follow Meeting** delivers personalized transcripts and summaries through My Notes for users who missed all or part of a Zoom meeting. Instead of asking three colleagues what happened or scrubbing a two-hour recording, employees get the context they need to move work forward. *(Expected December 2026.)*


**Screen Capture in Transcript** captures screenshots during the meeting and ties them to the exact moment in the My Notes transcript, so the slide or chart being discussed is preserved alongside the conversation and can be found later. When someone revisits a meeting, the context is not just what was said, but what was shown at the time. *(Expected December 2026.)*


### Capture context wherever conversations happen


The Unified Context Layer is only as good as the conversations feeding it. If it only captured Zoom Meetings, the picture might still be incomplete.


The new **My Notes standalone mobile app** can record and transcribe in-person meetings without requiring users to have the Zoom Workplace app, bringing the same meeting capture and summarization capabilities to hallway conversations, offsite meetings, and impromptu check-ins. For IT teams, this means fewer conversations fall off the record simply because they happened away from a screen. *(Expected December 2026.)*


**My Notes hardware integrations** with DTEN and Bota extend meeting intelligence further. The **DTEN Action Card** is a credit-card-sized device that turns any in-person conversation into My Notes with one press — no phone or laptop needed. Bota offers two devices that connect with My Notes: **Leaf** , a magnetic card for phone-based capture, and **Bean** , a wearable for hands-free recording. For IT teams managing hybrid environments, this means context does not disappear just because a conversation happened off-screen. *(DTEN expected November 2026; Bota expected Q1 2027.)*


And with Zoom's new headless approach, context does not need to stay locked inside the Zoom app. Conversation intelligence can be accessed via **MCP connectors and APIs** , allowing Zoom context to be used in other AI platforms like Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex. Starting in November, users will also be able to launch Zoom workflows directly from Claude and Codex — automating meeting, chat, and phone tasks and even updating CRM records — so that decisions and details are surfaceable wherever work is happening.


### Give AI agents the context to work with


The Unified Context Layer does not serve only people. It serves the AI agents working alongside them.


**[ZoomMate](https://www.zoom.com/en/products/ai-assistant/) Agent Teams** are specialized AI agents that work in parallel, coordinated by a team lead that assigns tasks and consolidates outputs into a deliverable for human review. Because these agents draw on the Unified Context Layer, they have access to conversational and document history behind a project, not the last meeting summary alone. The result is AI that can produce structured deliverables grounded in what happened across conversations, documents, and data. *(Available now.)*


**New Zoom Chat experience** surfaces what matters in a refreshed chat interface and brings AI agents directly into conversations to take approved actions. Administrator-defined controls govern what agents can and cannot do, so IT maintains oversight while employees get faster results. *(Expected December 2026.)*


**Search and Ask APIs** let developers and AI agents query the Unified Context Layer directly from connected third-party tools or MCP-compatible agents. For organizations building AI-powered workflows outside of Zoom, this means the context captured across meetings, chats, and calls becomes accessible wherever the workflow runs, not locked inside the Zoom UI. *(Available now.)*


### Governance that scales with the context layer


More context flowing through the system means more governance surface area. The Unified Context Layer is built with security and administrator controls that support access management. Centralized AI management, sensitivity labels that sync with Microsoft Purview, and account-level controls for AI agents are designed to help keep the context layer governed as it scales.


For a deeper look at Zoom's full security, AI guardrails, and compliance capabilities, see the companion security and trust blog (publishing shortly after Zoomtopia).


## From conversations to completed work


The pattern here is a shift IT leaders have been asking for: instead of deploying more tools and hoping employees connect the dots, the Unified Context Layer builds that connection into the platform. Context flows from conversations to documents to AI agents to follow-up actions, governed by the same admin controls IT already manages.


Zoom AI users report completing tasks twice as fast, with 72% reporting high or extremely high business impact (compared with a 63% market average).‡ Those numbers reflect what happens when collaboration is not only a communication channel, but a system that connects conversations to the work that follows.


"Before, our teams had the information they needed, but it was buried across meetings, notes, and different systems," said Christine Sarros, SVP, Enterprise Engineering at Oracle. "Now, when someone goes into a customer conversation, they can understand what was discussed previously, what was decided, and what still needs to happen. That means less time reconstructing history and more time actually moving the customer forward."


For IT teams evaluating their collaboration strategy, the question is no longer whether employees will use AI across meetings, chat, and phone. They already are. The question is whether the context behind all of those conversations connects to the workflows where business outcomes are produced, or disappears the moment the call ends.
